review_text: Great price. Was a gift. Very reasonably priced, and I've had really good luck with JVC products in the past. I wish JVC made more things.

Pleasantly surprised and happy with the product. I was (admittedly) apprehensive about buying the Halo after reading the reviews here and on Cnet but have been pleasantly surprised by the product. I've been using them for a good part of the day to listen to music and take conference calls from my PC..it fits my head just fine without any issue (I must have the Jabra "standard" head shape!). Sound is okay for work listening and the folks on the other end of my VoIP calls have reported normal voice quality.

***UPDATED*** I'm now a few weeks on of daily use and continue to be happy with the Halo!

PROS
* The touch volume slider is convenient and reasonably sensitive - not a selling point but it works.
* Sound quality - not too bassy or trebl-y. These do a reasonable job of blocking out ambient "office noise"
* Voice quality - I've used these on Skype and my mobile and folks on the other end still report good quality

CONS
* The inner headphone lining does tend to grab a bit of fuzz (a minor annoyance)

sounds good. Sound quality is excellent, really deep bass great midrange andand trebble, but the fit is lacking. The JBL's sound better than the Klipsch S4's that I was using before but the fit is uncomfortable.

The fit is great, but the sound is not. My Amazon purchase of Phillips earhook earphones SHS8100/28 had the potential to be the best earphones I ever owned, but missed the mark which is sad. They'll break in a year or less. I got my Halo at a Best Buy about a year ago. The headset has the upper piece that sits on top of the head and two lower pieces with the earphones that are connected to the upper piece by joints that have to be put together with a 'click'. Problem is, these joints are made of plastic and if they don't connect, the headset does not work. I use my headset every day. I like them. They have good sound. The joints have worn out, though, and my headset will not stay together anymore. A piece of plastic on one side cracked two months ago and recently fell off. It's winter now, too, so if I can finally manage to gingerly get the pieces together, after I put my hat on, they come apart. Most of the time you don't even know they've separated until you try to make a phone call or listen to music and realize the headset is not working. What a waste of a Benjamin for a headset to function properly for less than a year. They won't work with the PS3, either.

Great design. I bought these headphones after seeing my friend's pair. They're very aesthetically appealing (very subtle when you're wearing them and I've gotten a few compliments about how they look). There are also several common sense additions which make me happy. Firstly, they charge via an included micro usb cord, instead of a proprietary charger. Secondly, there is no obnoxious blinking blue light on at all times (like the Samsung SBH170). Thirdly, folding the headset up turns it off, and unfolding it turns it back on (and autosyncs). The interface is easy to figure out, although the double-tap to skip tracks feature is a little touchy. One thing to be careful of: the length of the headphones is adjustable, but not the curvature, so if you have a small head, the fit might be a little loose. Overall, I highly recommend this product. If you've never had bluetooth headphones before, it's great and this is a quality pair.

Only thing I wish was that the sub can be left on 100% of the time, it only kicks on at certain frequencies and the volume has to be a little loud to get it going. Other than that, these are awesome headphones at $47, would recommend them for some "fun" listening.

Third time's a charm. edit 1/26/16: I couldn't resist the feeling like I gave up on them too soon so I ordered directly from v-moda a white crossfade wireless. I'm going through a second trial. Really loving them so far. Comparing them to my m100 the bass is definitely tighter and in bluetooth mode there's almost more bass. I really prefer the refinements of this sound wired or wireless to the original m100. I still love the m100, but those have gone to my wife and these are mine now. In my original review I mentioned some hiss/sizzle - it turns out these headphones are so clear that they make some recordings' flaws completely apparent. Yes, in low volume there is a bluetooth hiss, but at high volume what I was hearing on many tracks was hiss in the recording. I a/b this back and forth with the m100 and cfw in wired mode and the hiss was there at high volumes. Don't get me wrong, maxed out there might be hiss from the internal amp being pushed, but that's to be expected on any device with its volume maxed. I'm really enjoying them this time around, I have one more headphone to try out but its $550 from master and dynamic - and at that price point it better sound twice as good as these, because if it doesn't i'm sticking with v-moda. I'm leaving my old review up just for comparison's sake. Still leaving it at four stars because theres no 4.5 option. They make my temple and jaw sore after a while in normal use, and almost instantly when lying down. Also, I thougth cliq fold being omitted would be an issue but honestly the carrying case is form fitting and fits in my gym bag just as easily. Its not as short, but its flatter than the m100 case. Plus I found myself not folding my m100 because the earpads would get squished and began to flatten out prematurely. I had to order replacements.

The V-Moda Crossfade wireless is difficult for me to review because ultimately I returned it and kept the m100. The two I received had battle scars from shipping. Both were sealed with the vmoda red ribbon and had the stickers over the earcups so i'm presuming they were brand new. However the first one had scratches on the silver trim between the earcup and earpad. The replacement had a scuff on the earcup and the microphone had shifted in its housing. If you looked inside the pinhole you could see the mic warped to the left. I think there was insufficient packing material in the box and it was bouncing around. Thats not VModas fault. So none of this reflects my rating. Just letting people know to inspect their expensive new toys! Now for the rating.

I loved the wired sound, and really liked the wireless sound. Wired it is very reminiscent of the m100 with slightly tighter bass, and slightly less of it too. Its gives a sense of a more balanced sound than the m100. It is pretty much V-moda sound signature just refined slightly. If you don't A/B them you wouldn't know there's a difference.

Wireless was great unless you turned the volume on the headphone itself up past half, Then there would be this distortion/sizzle/hiss at the top end of the sound regardless of how low the volume was on the music player. Up past half, to me - is where the amp really drove the headphones and made the bass thump, but that's where the sizzle lived. It was hard for me to find a balance between player/headphone volume. The bluetooth was also not dead quiet. I don't listen to music very loudly so I could always hear the signal noise. Its not a "bluetooth" thing in the sense that not every device suffers from this, but I've encountered it before. I have a bluetooth dongle right next to me that doesn't have this line level hiss at all. This was my ultimate reason for not replacing it another time after the second dud. I got my m100 for half the cost of the CFW; I wasn't going to pay double when the main feature was not up to standard. I believe they are almost there. If there's a CFW 2.0 Val will probably address all the signal quality issues with bluetooth. Until then i'm sticking with wired m100.

Minor concerns of mine were the battery life over time (year two and up), sweat/rain damaging the electronics, and falls. The physical build quality is as durable as the m100 but the electronics add more variables that could fail in the event of a minor fall/spill. I know people use bluetooth on the go,so if you're on a train and they fall or it starts to rain, would the destruction be covered under warranty? Too scary for me to take that change.

so why 4 stars? They're excellent headphones wired, if you find the balance in volumes they're very good in wireless mode. I can be objective enough to know that something is good even though its not good for me in particular.

Superb headphones!. So why am I giving headphones that I consider to be fantastic only 3 stars? Because I also happen to own the Plantronics Backbeat pros. Those headphones are superior in almost every way for the same price or far less if you get the older version.

I will focus first on these headphones and then the comparison to the Plantronics. The Crossfades scream quality and beauty when unboxing. The materials are the highest quality and they just feel good. The metal construction is top notch and the plastics are solid and substantial. The metal accent shields are beautiful and just make the headphones look good.

Controls are sparse, but effective. There is a power/pairing button on the bottom of the right headphone that functions well and is fairly intuitive. At the top are a series of three button. The center one pauses/starts the music and answers calls. The two surrounding it control volume and skip music forward or backward.

These headphones are very comfortable. I have a large head and they accommodate me with ease and I don't have too much discomfort even after a couple of hours use. They are even more comfortable after adding the XL pads. The pads make the ear opening larger and put more distance between the ear and the speaker. The XL pads are so much better that I think VMODA should have made them standard instead of selling them as an extra. Especially at this price point.

Sound. If I hadn't heard a better set, I would have been completely happy with this headphone. Bass is good and highs are where they should be. Mids are a bit too recessed for my taste so some vocals are lost. They play well at low volumes and can get plenty loud. Sound bleed is minimal and the outside world does not intrude too much. In the end, these really are great sounding headphones. Again, the XL pads improve the sound greatly. They provide a greater depth of sound and a much warmer tone.

This brings me to the reason that I am returning these and why they are only receiving 3 stars from me, despite how much I like them. I happen to own the Plantronics Backbeat Pro and they are superior to the Crossfades in nearly every way. The controls are more intuitive and easier to use. The Plantronics have APTx, active noise cancelling, voice prompts, and longer battery life. Most importantly, they simply sound better. As good as the Crossfades are, the Backbeats are better. Deeper bass, better mids, and they sound far clearer than the Crossfades. The Crossfades are very muddy by comparison. The Vmodas are constructed of better quality materials, are lighter, and look better, but that is not enough to justify buying them when a better alternative exists. Especially since you can get the old version of the Plantronics for far less.

To sum up. Great headphones that you will likely be really happy with, but there are better available for similar or less money. I also think that it is a sin that VMODA charges extra for the XL pads which are a necessity to get the best out of them. I really wanted to keep these and be happily ever after, but I simply can't. Back they go.

Side note that I owned a pair of the SkullCrushers in 11' and if I remember correctly they had a much better Bass frequency, didn't give spontaneous migraine headaches, and fit about the same as the Crushers with much more storing flexibility. Although they did lack in sound quality as these feel a bit crisper and more lively. I would still recommend the SkullCrushers to people who want to experience a ripe sub woofing right into their ear canals as opposed to the cerebral jack hammering the new Crushers give out.

Design Flaws Destroy its Value. The Jabra HALO is a very nice looking set of headphones. The sound quality is fine (I'm not picky though), but there are a number of design flaws that really make it a no-buy for me.

1. The only way to turn the headphones on and off is by folding in their right side. The power mechanism is built into the hinge. For someone who does a lot of on-and-off listening, it's really annoying to not be able to just turn the headphones off.

2. The folding arms are weak. After about a month of regular use, small cracks started to form around the hinges where the headphones fold. Now, after about three months, shards of plastic are constantly splitting off, and the hinges no longer stay open on their own. I have to carefully put the headphones on, and then the pressure from resting against my head keeps them in place. A moving part like this should have been designed to withstand much more wear and tear.

3. The touch-sensitive area on the right earpiece that does volume and next/previous track is terrible. It is sluggish and slow to respond. You'll also find that you accidentally change the volume a lot of the time when you're trying to reach the play/pause button, or trying to change tracks. Using a touch sensor here is pure gimmick, I would definitely prefer physical buttons.

4. If you have glasses, you'll be miserable. The headphones, although sleek, are really uncomfortable to wear for more than a few minutes if you're wearing glasses.

If these headphones cost $10.00, I wouldn't mind just buying a new pair every couple of months, but at over $50.00 I can't recommend them.

A refined M-100 with wireless capabilities? Oh yes!. V-Moda is a brand that has always been very fashion forward. It was until the M80 and M100 in which they were able take traction and gain popularity by merging their designs with respectable acoustics that was generally pleasing to a wide range of people. Now, they have finally taken what made them popular and removed the wires. This is the new Crossfade Wireless.

The box is a bit taller than the M100’s version because there is no longer the click fold hinge that allowed the headphone to collapse in upon self, rendering the new Crossfade wireless not as portable. This may be a deal breaker to some, but the included case is still of quality and attempts to minimize its footprint by molding its shape to the headphone. Included in the box is a spare set of shields usually this will be the custom set you’ve created. You have your quick guide and warranty information especially informing you about V-Moda’s kick ass immortal life program. Inside the specially molded clamshell zipper case you’ll find the micro USB cable to charge your headphones and the 1 button with an in-line microphone cable allowing you to use the Crossfade wireless in passive mode in the event the battery dies or you simply yearn for the best possibly sound quality. And at last you have the clip to mount the case on a bag or your belt.

The Crossfade Wireless retains the same incredibly rugged and sexy design as the M-100 and LP series. What’s even more amazing is that it keeps the same size even despite now housing internal electronics to allow wireless connectivity. I have the XL pads installed and these offer improved cushion depth, a bigger soundstage and a smoother sound as well a wider ear diameter for superior comfort over the stock pads. A much recommended upgrade. The headband offers substantial padding to avoid hot points at the top of the head and remains aesthetically pleasing by not being overly bulky and/or not aligning to the curvature of your head. In summary, these are gorgeous, well-built headphones that can easily withstand everyday wear and tear and if you do break them, the immortal life program is an option.
The location of the wireless controls are fairly intuitive. On the top left we have the volume down button. On the top middle, we have the multi button, play, pause, answer and reject calls as well as activating your voice assistant and on the top right we have the volume up button. Moving down we have a single rocker that when pushed to the middle turns on the headphone and pairs it to the last known device and when pushed and held to the far right for 2-3 seconds puts it in pairing mode. The Crossfade wireless can be connected to 2 devices at once, for example a smart watch and a smart phone or a smart phone and a tablet.

The M-100 was at a time my favorite headphone, but it was until I ventured off into what other high quality portable offerings were available that made me see its flaws. The M-100 is undeniably a pleasing and fun sounding headphone with stunning bass performance, but its resolution and coherency leaved some to be desired. The Crossfade Wireless is a welcoming improvement. By taking the famous M-100 sound and fine tuning the frequency response balance to be more linear as well as brining out more resolving power to allow the subtle textures and harmonic low level details to surface has resulted in being my favorite Bluetooth headphone, period and possibly being my overall “favorite” sounding headphone surpassing the Master & Dynamic MH40. Yes, these are that DAMN good. When in Bluetooth operation, the following said about the sound quality of the Crossfade Wireless is still mostly the same, but it just doesn’t have the same level of detail and overall focus as when it is wired and plugged into a fine setup. Other than that, these are the best sounding Bluetooth headphones I have heard and owned surpassing the Parrot Zik 2, Sennheiser Momentum Wireless, Sony XB950BT, Bang & Olufsen H8, Definitive Technology Symphony 1, Beats Studio Wireless, Beats Solo2 Wireless, Samsung Level Over and Bowers & Wilkins P5 Wireless. I've got no strings on me!. I love running with over-ear headphones, and lately my Crossfade M-100s have been my go-to cans for that. The one thing that I've always hated while running with any headphones is dealing with the cords - pulling earbuds out of my ears, rubbing and getting in the way of arm movement with on-ear or over-ear, etc. I can tuck them in my shirt or whatever, but then they're annoying and pull when I turn my head. And let's be honest - most cordless headphones sound like garbage. Been there, done that, returned it. Yeah, first world problems but why not shoot for perfection? The only reason I even gave these a shot is because they're V-MODA and I'm not just surprised, I'm blown away.

V-MODA claims that these sound equivalent to wired headphones. I'm going to disagree for my most common use case - connected directly to my iPhone 6S. In this case, they sound a bit better. The integrated amplified delivers more and cleaner bass presence than my iPhone can. Not as good as with a standalone DAC/amp, but I'd say about 30% better than the iPhone alone - which is not a subtle improvement, and without the distortions introduced by the iPhone's electronic equalizer. You can practically see the strings on a bass guitar vibrating in your mind, and the bass drums have a beautiful kick. Highs and mids still feature V-MODA's trademark clarity and nice, even frequency response. So yes, the sound is wonderful, which is what everyone really cares about. I've seen some complaints in forums, but as far as I can tell these have been narrowed down to devices that just can't send good quality audio over Bluetooth. I haven't personally had any issues yet, but I've only tested with my iPhone and MacBook Pro. Charging is accomplished with a standard micro-USB cable, so most people won't have to worry about carrying extra cords or chargers to keep the Crossfade Wireless topped up while traveling. Battery life hasn't yet been an issue. They come with a typically excellent V-MODA travel case, the sort that puts every other brand to shame but V-MODA buyers have become pleasantly used to.

Minor quibbles:
* No cliq-fold hinges like the M-100s and XS. Sorry, V-MODA, you spoiled us and it's hard to go back.
* A single button for pause / resume / track-forward / track-back. I suck at pressing these fast enough, so I always wind up just pausing it.

I'm pretty nit-picky about things, so that's a pretty short list. I'm loving these so far!

These three buttons feel flimsy to me and for worse, they are kind of hard to press, for some reason presenting resistance particularly when I try to turn the volume down. Perhaps they made it this way to avoid accidental pressing, but these buttons are right underneath the metal clip that holds the band to the cans so I'd imagine it would be somewhat difficult to bump into something that would hit the buttons here.

On the inside, we have a whole new story. If you're coming from the M-100, these are supposed to sound the same. Even after burn-in, the sound felt almost hollow to me, compared to the M-100. The bass was lacking, both on bluetooth and wireless, which is what most seem to buy V-Modas for. The mids were recessed, but this is no change from the M-100. The highs were also present, so no change here. Somewhere along the line, V-Moda tweaked these headphones and dropped (upped?) the bass from the M-100s. These headphones also lack aptX lossless/low-latency codec which is a major disappointment in this price range. The Sony MDR10BT has it and costs less. What gives, V-Moda?

The other thing to note in regards to the bluetooth is that if you listen to softer music, you may notice a near-silent static playing along with your music. This seems to be the standard for bluetooth headphones.

Other notes:
- The micro USB charging port is on the LEFT cup, while the 3.5mm plug is on the RIGHT cup. I prefer my wire on the left side, so this is entirely up to user preference.
- These lose the cliquefold mechanism that was so popular with the M-100. Bluetooth is intended for mobility, so it's strange that this would get removed, but it may be a design limitation here. If you're coming from the M-100, expect the larger LP case.
- These can be paired and connected with more than one device at a time, but can only play one at a time. This is pretty interesting, since the M-100s had two ports so that you could either listen to two sources at once or daisy chain your headphones. Unfortunately you can not stream to the cans and use the 3.5mm port as an audio-out.
- If you have the M-100s, or really any headphones that have a removable audio-in cable and want wireless, I'd check out these: [[ASIN:B0134DTP9Q BTunes VXB-35 (3.5mm Model) To Make Wired Headphones Wireless for Beats, Monster, Sony, V-Moda, Marshalls and more]]. I'm ended up returning my Crossfade Wireless and buying this instead.

Now, over all audio quality. I'm picky about my audio quality. Picky enough where I can't stand not having an equalizer I can tweak to my liking, but I don't think it's quite fair to call myself an audiophile. That said, the over all audio quality seems fine to me. I did have a headset that was cheap, but supposed professionals were claiming they had really good audio quality despite the price. Comparing the two, I can tell a difference in audio, but not so much in quality. I couldn't tell you which ones sound better over all, I think it comes down more to preference unless you're doing super high end professional work where it's an absolute must to have sensitive headphones to pick apart audio at the seems. The main thing I seek in audio is heavy bass and these deliver, the non-bass audio sounds perfectly good too so over all I'm very happy.
